# Agent instructions

Read the applicable shared Lunchbox Labs standards before editing this repository:

- [Common agent guidance](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/common.md)
- [Workflow conventions](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/workflows.md)
- [npm package conventions](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/npm-packages.md)
- [Agent tooling conventions](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/agent-tooling.md)
- [State machine conventions](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/state-machines.md)

These documents must be read explicitly; GitHub does not automatically inherit them here.

## Layout

This repository is an npm workspace with one lockfile and two published packages released together at one version:

- `packages/core` (`@lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-core`, private): discovery, include expansion, the server hooks, the prompt viewer and the host profiles in `src/host.ts`, with the unit tests. It is never published and has no runtime dependency on a host package.
- `packages/opencode` (`@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer`) and `packages/kilo` (`@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer`): thin adapters that pass their host profile to the core and ship their host's examples in `docs/examples/`. Their build bundles the core with tsdown (`tsdown.config.mjs` at the root), keeping every other import external, so they don't depend on it.

Put host differences in the host profile as data rather than in branches. Root `tests/` holds the package, native, example, release and baseline tests, and `tests/hosts.ts` describes each host for them. Shared tooling and its configuration live at the root.

## Commands

`npm run check` runs static checks and the unit tests of every package. Run `npm run test:package` separately for packed-package validation of both hosts, and `npm run test:native` for native integration; set `NATIVE_HOST=kilo` for Kilo CLI, and `OPENCODE_TEST_VERSION` or `KILO_TEST_VERSION` for a version lane.

## Documentation

The GitHub wiki is published from `docs/wiki/`: the Wiki workflow replaces the wiki with that folder on every push to `main` that changes it, so edit pages there, never in the wiki itself. Each file is one page named after its filename, with `_Sidebar.md` as the sidebar; link pages by name, as in `[Usage](Usage)`. Keep in-depth user and developer guides in the wiki, and the root and package READMEs to a short introduction that links to them.

Write documentation for knowledgeable OpenCode and Kilo CLI users: explain plugin-specific concepts without host or package-install basics or unnecessary cautions. Keep installation examples simple and unversioned. Use short, relevant README snippets and put full, simple, realistic examples in each adapter's `docs/examples/`. Keep maintainer publishing and release-process walkthroughs out of the README and user pages; the wiki's Developer pages hold them, and release notes are still appropriate.

The plugin's state machines are documented in [docs/state-machines.md](docs/state-machines.md). Update it in the same PR as any change to their states, triggers or exits, with tests for each transition and failure path the change adds or alters.

## Contributor workflows

For authoring, diagnostics, examples, viewer or restart behavior changes, request an independent `opencode-user-review`, and `kilo-user-review` when Kilo CLI users are affected. For discovery, include expansion, native prompt ownership, skill-body or host integration changes, request an independent `composition-contract-review`. Use both when both areas change; skip unrelated roles. Give reviewers the diff/base and relevant test or runtime evidence.

Use `.agents/skills/native-package-verification/SKILL.md` for applicable package/native checks. These contributor workflows do not require the plugin or alter the shipped examples. The [agent tooling conventions](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/agent-tooling.md) cover the file layout, invocation in each tool and reviewer permissions.
@AGENTS.md

---
name: composition-contract-review
description: Use when discovery, include expansion, native agent or command composition, skill bodies, or host integration changes.
---

Review the supplied diff against the composition contract and existing tests. Read packages/core/src/host.ts, discovery.ts, include-core.ts, runtime.ts, skill-body.ts and server.ts, the adapters under packages/opencode/src and packages/kilo/src, and the affected tests as relevant. Do not edit files or execute mutating commands; request missing runtime evidence from the implementing agent.

Trace the actual loaded body, not only configuration registration. Check discovery order and duplicate-path precedence for each host profile, project-config disabling, startup snapshots, recursive required/optional includes, escaping, edge trimming and surrounding whitespace. Optional includes may disappear silently only when absent from every discovered root. Every other include problem (malformed or unsafe paths, unreadable or invalid files, cycles, count and depth limits) leaves out only that include, keeps a malformed marker literal and shows a warning; the composed-size limit keeps the consumer's native text. One consumer's problems never block another, hooks never reject over include or discovery problems, and unsafe paths are still never read.

Check path containment (including symlinks), supported file types, cycle detection, depth/count/byte limits, and consumer/source diagnostics. Use current constants and tests rather than inventing limits. Check agent prompts and command templates retain native ownership and non-prompt fields, including arguments and shell syntax.

Verify skill bodies through the native skill tool. Generated skill slash commands do not expand includes, and the prompt viewer does not expose skills. Issue #102 was closed because no reliable supported hook exists: do not propose an unsupported hook or brittle interception as a fix. Distinguish native host evidence from mocked hook/unit evidence.

Return only supported findings, ordered by impact, with location, triggering input, evidence, resulting behavior and minimal correction. State no findings when appropriate, with any untested host/version boundaries. Do not treat missing runtime evidence as a proven bug.

---
name: kilo-user-review
description: Use when changes affect prompt authoring, diagnostics, examples, the prompt viewer, or restart expectations.
---

Review the supplied diff and affected flows as a knowledgeable Kilo user. Read relevant source, README, examples, and test evidence. Do not edit files or run commands that mutate the project; ask the implementing agent for missing runtime evidence.

Trace a realistic task from writing a shared snippet through including it in a native agent, command, or on-demand skill. Check whether discovery and overrides are understandable, failures identify the affected consumer/include and a useful correction, and optional includes distinguish absence from invalid input.

For viewer changes, inspect /view-prompts navigation, Agents/Commands selection, built-in visibility, scrolling, long-text parts, empty/error states, and back/close behavior. Skills are omitted from the viewer; skill-tool composition does not imply slash-command composition. Check that guidance explains restarting the Kilo server after editing snippets or native definitions.

Separate source inference, test output, screenshots, and observed runtime behavior. Do not claim real user testing or accessibility certification from source review. Read available screenshots or logs; explicitly state what could not be exercised.

Return actionable findings ordered by impact: location, concrete scenario, evidence, user impact, and smallest useful correction. Avoid style preferences and speculative findings. There is no finding quota; if none are supported, say so and list meaningful verification gaps.

Run npm run check for static and unit checks. Run npm run test:package for exports or distribution changes; inspect the packed file list and exercise the packed package rather than relying on source imports. Keep root .agents, .codex, .claude, .opencode, .kilo and CLAUDE.md contributor files out of every package, and tests and sources out of the core package. Preserve packages/opencode/docs/examples and packages/kilo/docs/examples as shipped product examples.

Run npm run test:native for host, composition, or viewer changes. Inspect its setup first: it resolves and installs the supported host named by NATIVE_HOST (opencode by default, or kilo) and uses isolated fixtures. Run each host a change can affect, using the existing OPENCODE_TEST_VERSION or KILO_TEST_VERSION lanes when needed, without weakening the compatibility baseline. Follow the existing harness; do not invoke paid model/API calls. Report unavailable dependencies, hosts, or blocked checks rather than replacing native evidence with a mock.

Inspect actual loaded agent/command text and skill-tool bodies, plus viewer behavior where affected. Configuration presence alone does not prove body composition. Verify required, recursive, optional and escaped includes against the relevant existing cases; generated skill slash commands remain outside the composition contract. Restart the server between changed startup definitions.

Report commands, exit results, host/version and lane, observed loaded-body/package evidence, and any skipped or unavailable checks. Distinguish source inference, unit/packed tests and native runtime observations. Keep detailed task evidence on the linked issue, not in committed plan documents.

# Prompt Composer

Share reusable prompt text across native agents, commands and on-demand skills with explicit inline includes, in OpenCode and Kilo CLI.

| Host | Package |
| --- | --- |
| OpenCode | [`@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer`](packages/opencode/) |
| Kilo CLI | [`@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer`](packages/kilo/) |

Both packages are built from the shared source in [`packages/core`](packages/core/), which the build bundles into each of them; it is not published on its own. Each package README shows how to install it, and the [wiki](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/wiki) has the full guides.

# Prompt Composer core

The source that the [OpenCode](../opencode/) and [Kilo CLI](../kilo/) packages share: prompt discovery, include expansion, the server hooks, the prompt viewer, and a host profile for each host in `src/host.ts`.

This package is private and is never published. Each host package's build bundles it with [tsdown](https://tsdown.dev/), so the published packages don't depend on it. Its `exports` point at the TypeScript sources, for the host packages' build and typecheck within the workspace; its version is not released.

[Developer](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/wiki/Developer) describes the workspace.

# Kilo Prompt Composer

Share reusable prompt text across native Kilo CLI agents, commands and on-demand skills with explicit inline includes.

Requires Node **22.18+**. Tested with Kilo CLI **7.8.x**, starting at **7.8.27**.

## Install

Add the package to `plugin` in `kilo.jsonc`, and to `tui.jsonc` for the prompt viewer:

```jsonc
{ "plugin": ["@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer"] }
```

## Include shared text

Write shared text in `.kilo/prompts/review.md`:

```markdown
Check the implementation and report actionable findings with evidence.
```

Include it where it belongs in an agent prompt, command template or skill body:

```markdown
Review the supplied changes.

{{include:review.md}}

Distinguish observed behavior from assumptions.
```

Use `{{include?:personal/review.md}}` for an include that may be absent, and run `/view-prompts` to read the loaded agent and command text. Restart the Kilo server after editing snippets. A problem with an include shows a warning toast and never stops a prompt from loading; [Usage](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/wiki/Usage#snippet-lifetime) describes what is kept.

# Review guidance

This project contains a native `review` agent, a `/check` command and shared prompt snippets. Register the plugin in `kilo.jsonc`, and in `tui.jsonc` for `/view-prompts`, then open this folder as the project.

The agent includes review context before its task and the findings format within its body. `/check` uses the same findings snippet after `Review $ARGUMENTS.`. These inline includes determine ordering; there is no separate agent-rule settings file. The files under `.kilo/` are the complete, runnable source.

Select `review` or run `/check`, and use `/view-prompts` to inspect the loaded agent and command text. After changing snippets, restart the Kilo server. To override a shared snippet, use the same relative filename in a later prompt root; see [Discovery](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/wiki/Discovery).

# On-demand verification

This project contains a native `verification` skill and a reusable checklist in `.kilo/prompts/verification.md`.

Register the plugin, open this folder as the project and ask the agent to load `verification` through the native skill tool. Prompt Composer expands the include in the returned skill body while preserving the host wrapper. The automatically generated skill slash command does not expand includes.

The checklist is captured when the project first initializes in the server process, even if the skill is loaded later. Restart the server after editing it. Kilo owns skill discovery and permissions. This is a project example; the package does not install global help skills.

# State machines

This document describes the state Prompt Composer keeps across hooks, events and reloads. Update it in the same PR as any change to these states, their triggers or their exits, following the [state machine conventions](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/state-machines.md), and cover each transition you add or change in `packages/core/tests/`. Paths below are relative to `packages/core`, which the build bundles into both host packages. Known bugs belong in issues, not here.

OpenCode and Kilo rerun the server plugin's factory on every instance load but keep the imported module, so module-level state lasts for the process and closure state is rebuilt on each reload. The bundle emits each core module once per package, so a package has one copy of each module-level state; a module that several entries use, such as the include engine and its error classes, goes to a chunk they share. Every state below is the same for both hosts except where a host profile (`src/host.ts`) is named.

## Snippet capture cache

`snapshots` in `src/startup-snippets.ts` maps each host name and resolved directory and worktree pair to the promise of its capture. `startupSnippets` returns the existing promise for a key, so every factory for the same project and host shares one capture until the host restarts, and two hosts never share one. The capture resolves the host's home and custom config directory once, when it starts; the Kilo profile trims surrounding whitespace from the home directory first, as Kilo does.

- The first factory for a key starts `capture()`.
- A capture that resolves, with or without warnings, is kept for the rest of the process.
- A capture that rejects, which in practice means `discoveryDirectories` failed (the ancestor limit, or an unexpected `lstat` error on a project config directory such as `.opencode`, `.kilocode` or `.kilo`), is evicted so a later factory captures again. Every factory that received the promise while it was pending keeps the rejection, so its config hooks keep the native prompts with an error toast until the next reload.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Absent
    Absent --> Capturing: first factory for the project
    Capturing --> Resolved: capture() returns
    Capturing --> Rejected: discovery throws
    Rejected --> Absent: evicted
    Resolved --> Resolved: later factories and reloads reuse it
    Resolved --> [*]: process exit
```

## Capture attempts

`capture()` makes up to `CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS` (3) attempts. Each one discovers files leniently, reads each file into a source or an error, then confirms nothing changed:

- Successful reads are re-read; one that now differs or fails is a change.
- Failed reads are then read again, as when an editor was saving the file mid-read. A read that failed because the file was replaced between being checked and opened is always a change; any other failed read is a change when it now succeeds or fails with a different message. A failure that repeats unchanged, such as an invalid or unreadable file, is kept.
- The inventory is discovered again; a different set of discovered directories, names or paths is a change.

A change starts another attempt. On the last attempt the latest reads are kept with a warning to restart the host (named by its profile) once edits settle. The result is frozen inside the `expand` closure, and an error entry is thrown again each time an include uses it; an entry for a file that was still being replaced says to restart the host once edits settle, since every later hook reuses the capture.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Attempt
    Attempt --> [*]: discovery throws, capture rejects
    Attempt --> Verify
    Verify --> Attempt: reads, failed reads or inventory changed, attempts left
    Verify --> Published: unchanged, repeated failures kept
    Verify --> PublishedWithWarning: changed on the last attempt, restart warning
    Published --> [*]
    PublishedWithWarning --> [*]
```

## Server plugin instance

Each factory run in `src/server.ts` holds:

- `startup`: the shared capture promise for this project.
- `firstConfig`: true until the first config hook, so option and capture warnings are toasted once per instance.
- `snapshots`: a `WeakMap` from a config object to its native and applied bodies, so a second config hook on the same object restores the native bodies before composing again.
- `warnedSkillCommands`: the skill commands already warned about in this instance, empty after each reload.

The config hook awaits `startup`. If it rejected, the hook shows an error toast and leaves the config unchanged. Otherwise it composes, shows any warnings, writes `config.agent` and `config.command` and records the snapshot. `tool.execute.after` for the skill tool expands includes in skill output from the same frozen capture, or returns the native output with a toast.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Fresh: factory
    Fresh --> AwaitCapture: config hook
    AwaitCapture --> NativeKept: capture rejected, error toast
    AwaitCapture --> Composed: compose ok
    NativeKept --> AwaitCapture: later config hook, rejects again
    Composed --> AwaitCapture: later config hook, native restored first on the same object
    Composed --> Composed: skill output expanded or kept with a toast
```

`command.execute.before` never changes the command and never throws. When a command's text or subtask prompt holds an include marker and the host lists the command with `source: "skill"`, the first such run of each skill in the instance shows a warning toast that its markers were sent as written; later runs of that skill are silent until a reload, so the diagram below is kept per skill. Configured commands, other sources, commands without markers and a command list that cannot be read never warn, and a command without markers is not looked up.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Unwarned: factory
    Unwarned --> Unwarned: no marker, not a skill command, or lookup failed
    Unwarned --> Warned: skill command with markers, warning toast
    Warned --> Warned: later runs of the same skill, no toast
    Warned --> [*]: instance reload
    Unwarned --> [*]: instance reload
```

## Composition and expansion

These have no state that outlives one call:

- Composition (`src/runtime.ts`) gives each agent or command one outcome: composed, composed with warnings, native kept (an empty result with problems, or `expand` threw, for example at the size limit), or skipped (an agent that is disabled or whose prompt is blank or not a string, or a command whose template is not a string).
- Include expansion (`src/include-core.ts`) tracks an include count, `limitReported` and the recursion stack for cycle checks. An escaped marker is written literally, a malformed one is left as written with a warning, a failing one expands to nothing with a warning, and exceeding `promptSize` throws an `IncludeError` that the caller turns into a fallback.
- The skill output gate (`src/skill-body.ts`) is a chain of checks. Every exit except a successful expansion returns the native output, with a toast unless nothing needed doing. After the metadata check it takes one of two framing branches: when the host profile has a `builtinSkillDirectory` (Kilo's `builtin`) and the metadata `dir` equals it, the body must end at the closing tag; otherwise the body must end before the base-directory and sampled-file footer. A built-in output that does not match its framing exits with the unknown-framing notice, and the OpenCode profile never takes the built-in branch.
- Discovery (`src/discovery.ts`) counts entries and, in lenient mode, leaves out entries that fail with `leaveOut`. `EntryLimitError` stops the walk and becomes one warning.

## TUI dialog navigation

`src/navigation.ts` keeps `frames`, `revision`, `replacing` and `visible`.

- `show` pushes a frame (a root frame resets first) and displays it. Displaying increments `revision` and replaces the host dialog with `replacing` set, so the host's close callback for the previous dialog is ignored.
- When the host closes the current dialog (Escape, OK or Cancel), the top frame is popped and a microtask redisplays the parent, unless the route, client, directory or lifecycle changed or another dialog is open, in which case navigation resets.
- Back pops and redisplays the parent, or closes with fewer than two frames. `refresh` redisplays the top frame and `close` resets and clears the dialog.
- `checkpoint` captures the revision, client, path and route; picker callbacks check it so callbacks from a retired dialog do nothing.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Closed
    Closed --> Showing: show
    Showing --> Showing: show child, refresh, back with a parent
    Showing --> Restoring: host closes the dialog
    Restoring --> Showing: context unchanged and a parent exists
    Restoring --> Closed: no parent or context changed
    Showing --> Closed: close, back at root, instance disposed
    Showing --> Detached: lifecycle abort resets without clearing the host dialog
    Detached --> Closed: user closes it
```

## /view-prompts load

`src/tui.ts` shows a "Loading prompts" alert and takes a checkpoint. A stale checkpoint (the alert was dismissed, the viewer reopened, or the route, client or directory changed) ends silently. A failed request or a throw shows a retry menu whose Retry loads again. Success shows the root menu, and navigation takes over.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Loading: /view-prompts
    Loading --> Loading: /view-prompts again
    Loading --> Idle: checkpoint stale
    Loading --> RetryMenu: request error or throw
    Loading --> RootMenu: ok
    RetryMenu --> Loading: Retry
    RetryMenu --> Idle: Escape
    RootMenu --> Idle: Escape at root
```

## Persisted and lifecycle state

- The `prompt-composer.showBuiltins` kv value is read once per open; toggling it writes kv and refreshes. A missing kv store reads as false.
- The fixed menu and text viewer renderables go from created to focused on a 1 ms timer and are destroyed by the host or a lifecycle abort. The fixed menu then clears its focus timer and abort listener; the text viewer also removes its resize listener and keymap layer.
- The TUI plugin registers the `/view-prompts` command and a `server.instance.disposed` watcher that closes an open viewer for the same directory, and unregisters both on dispose.

# Developer documentation

For contributors and maintainers working on Prompt Composer:

- [Workspace layout](#workspace-layout), [local builds and checks](#build-a-local-package): the packages, local builds, runtime boundaries and compatibility checks.
- [Publishing](Publishing): trusted publisher setup and the release workflow.

The plugin's state machines are documented in [docs/state-machines.md](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/docs/state-machines.md). These wiki pages are published from [docs/wiki](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/tree/main/docs/wiki) on every push to `main` that changes them; change them there.

The repository's [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and linked shared standards remain the authoritative machine instructions. Runnable examples and the license stay in the repository and the published adapter packages. [User documentation](Home#user-documentation) covers installation and everyday use.

Prompt Composer's include safety engine and dialog navigation originated in the MIT-licensed [Config Composer](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/opencode-config-composer) project. Configuration composition belongs to Config Composer, and inline prompt inclusion to Prompt Composer.

## Workspace layout

The repository is an npm workspace with one lockfile. Its two host packages are released together at one version, and both are built from a private core:

| Directory | Package | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/core` | `@lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-core` (private, not published) | Discovery, include expansion, the server hooks, the prompt viewer, the host profiles in `src/host.ts`, and the unit tests |
| `packages/opencode` | `@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer` | The OpenCode adapter and its examples |
| `packages/kilo` | `@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer` | The Kilo CLI adapter and its examples |

A host profile holds what differs between hosts as data: the product name in messages, the global, project and home config directories, the environment variables, whether the home directory is trimmed and line breaks are removed from `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (Kilo only), and the metadata of built-in skills. The core takes a profile in `createServer` and `createTui`, and each adapter passes its own and re-exports the result with the host's plugin types. The core has no runtime dependency on a host package.

Each adapter's `npm run build` bundles the core into it with [tsdown](https://tsdown.dev/), using the shared [`tsdown.config.mjs`](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/tsdown.config.mjs). The `server`, `includes` and `tui` entries build to `dist/<entry>.js` and `dist/<entry>.d.ts` in one build, so each core module is emitted once per package: a module that more than one entry uses, such as the include engine and its error classes, goes to a shared chunk rather than being copied into each entry. The build also fails when an entry's declaration file declares no exports. Every other import stays external: Node built-ins, the host's `@opentui/core` that the viewer loads on demand, and the host plugin types in the declarations. The build fails if it would bundle anything from `node_modules` or emit any other import. npm links the core into the root `node_modules` as a workspace, so the adapters list no dependency on it, and the published manifests name no package that isn't on npm.

The OpenCode adapter builds against `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode-ai/sdk` 1.19.5 with `@opentui/*` 0.4.5, and the Kilo adapter against `@kilocode/plugin` and `@kilocode/sdk` 7.8.27 with `@opentui/*` 0.5.11. The [baseline tests](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/tree/main/tests) check these pins in the manifests and lockfile, and the Kilo package's `typecheck` script also typechecks the core sources against the Kilo pins: `packages/kilo/tsconfig.core.json` maps the core's `@opencode-ai/plugin` imports to `@kilocode/plugin` and `@opentui/*` to the Kilo package's nested 0.5.11 copies, so `npm run check:static` fails when the core stops matching either host's plugin API. Linting, formatting, TypeScript settings and the integration tests are shared at the root, and `tests/hosts.ts` describes each host for them.

## Build a local package

Use the committed npm lockfile. CI uses Node 24; the packages require Node 22.18 or later.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm pack --workspace packages/opencode --workspace packages/kilo
```

`npm run build` builds both adapters. Install the tarball for your host into a separate directory; it has no dependency to install alongside it. Register that installed adapter's absolute directory in `opencode.jsonc` or `kilo.jsonc` and, when testing the viewer, `tui.jsonc`. The host selects the corresponding server or TUI export. This exercises a local candidate without publishing it.

## Runtime boundaries

The server composes native agent and command bodies through the config hook and skill bodies through the skill tool's after hook. It preserves host metadata and publishes no partially composed config. The TUI reads loaded config and agent metadata; it does not write files or execute prompts.

Startup snippet capture is shared by normalized project context for the lifetime of the imported module. Instance disposal can rerun plugin factories without resetting that capture; a fresh process loads changed snippets. The separately exported `includes` API reads files when called. Keep these distinct lifetime contracts when changing the implementation.

Composition degrades instead of failing: a failing include expands to nothing, a malformed marker stays literal, and a consumer over the 256 KiB limit or left empty keeps its native text, each with a warning toast and a server log entry. Past the include count limit, only the first limit problem is reported. Consumers compose independently, hooks do not reject, and discovery used by startup capture skips unusable entries. A failed capture is not cached, so the next plugin factory captures again. The exported `includes` API and discovery without a skip callback keep their strict behavior.

The skill parser isolates the body from native framing and leaves names, directories and sampled filenames literal. When include markers are present, truncated output, unknown or ambiguous framing, or missing or invalid native name and directory metadata leaves the native output unchanged so the skill still loads; a warning toast explains that its includes were not expanded. Kilo's built-in skills, whose metadata `dir` is `builtin`, use a shorter wrapper without the sampled-file footer, and only the Kilo profile accepts it. Exact wrapper strings in tests protect this host boundary.

## Checks

| Command | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run check` | Typechecking, lint, formatting and the unit tests of every package |
| `npm run test:package` | For each host: installation of the packed package outside the workspace, every export's runtime use and declarations, and that the package neither depends on nor installs the core and inlines no third-party code |
| `npm run test:native` | Real host server, npm plugin loading, skill execution, process restart and terminal viewer, for the host in `NATIVE_HOST` |

`npm run test:native` runs OpenCode by default; set `NATIVE_HOST=kilo` for Kilo CLI. The native suite uses isolated configuration and a local model fixture; no provider account is needed. On Kilo it also disables telemetry and limits both the primary and the small model to the fixture provider. It downloads the host and verifies the ripgrep prerequisite. Some viewer checks replace rendering, while the PTY/ConPTY path exercises real terminal interaction and asserts that browsing sends no model request. Preserve both layers.

Tests should protect observable behavior, safety boundaries and host contracts. Use existing representative paths instead of duplicating wording or increasing test counts. The [shared standards](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/.github/blob/main/agent-guidance/common.md#meaningful-tests) define the testing policy.

## Host compatibility

The authoritative ranges and floors live in [tests/opencode.json](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/tests/opencode.json) and [tests/kilo.json](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/tests/kilo.json); they are separate from pinned SDK/build dependencies and are not shipped in the packages. No host runtime engine restriction is declared.

| Host | CLI package | Version lane variable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenCode | `opencode-ai` | `OPENCODE_TEST_VERSION` |
| Kilo CLI | `@kilocode/cli` | `KILO_TEST_VERSION` |

By default, native tests fetch fresh canonical metadata for the host's CLI package, choose the newest stable version in that range and install the exact platform binary. They verify the actual CLI version and fail on registry or artifact errors instead of using stale fallback versions. Set the lane variable to `floor` for the configured floor, or to an exact version inside the range.

[Check CI](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml) covers Linux and Windows, both hosts, and latest-compatible and floor versions. OpenCode also runs a Config Composer-first registration; Config Composer is an OpenCode plugin, so Kilo runs standalone only. For coexistence, build the Config Composer revision pinned in that workflow and set `CONFIG_COMPOSER_DIR` to its checkout before running `npm run test:native`. Its fixture follows that baseline's configuration format; substituting current Config Composer main requires a separate fixture compatibility review.

Each package's plugin and SDK dev dependencies (`@opencode-ai/*` 1.19.5 or `@kilocode/*` 7.8.27), and its `@opentui/*` and `solid-js` dev dependencies, stay on exact versions that match what its host bundles; the baseline tests enforce them. Other dependencies use version ranges, and `package-lock.json` decides what CI installs. Shared tooling at the root uses `^`, except TypeScript and Prettier, which use `~` because their minor releases change type checking and formatting. The npm version in the Release workflow's publish job also stays exact.

# Discovery

Prompt Composer discovers `prompts/` under the host's configuration directories. It follows this order:

1. The global XDG config directory: `~/.config/opencode` for OpenCode, or `~/.config/kilo` for Kilo, unless `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is absolute.
2. Existing project config directories, starting at the opened directory and ascending through the worktree. Non-Git projects ascend to the filesystem root. OpenCode reads `.opencode`; Kilo reads `.kilocode` and then `.kilo` at each level.
3. The same config directories under the home directory, when present.
4. The custom config directory variable, when set.

| | OpenCode | Kilo CLI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global directory | `opencode` | `kilo` |
| Project and home directories | `.opencode` | `.kilocode`, then `.kilo` |
| Custom config directory | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `KILO_CONFIG_DIR` |
| Disable project discovery | `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG` | `KILO_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG` |
| Home override used by host tests | `OPENCODE_TEST_HOME` | `KILO_TEST_HOME` |

Duplicate directory paths retain their first occurrence. Later files win collisions by relative filename, including nested names such as `review/findings.md`. A worktree-root config directory can override a descendant's; at each Kilo level `.kilo` overrides `.kilocode`. Home and custom config directories follow project directories. Setting the disable variable to `true` or `1` disables project discovery while retaining the other roots. Each package reads only its own host's directories and variables, so the Kilo package ignores `.opencode` and `OPENCODE_*`, and the OpenCode package ignores the Kilo ones.

This mirrors the host's agent/command directory order. It does not scan `.agents`, `.claude`, remote skill URLs or arbitrary skill paths for snippets. The host discovers native component definitions; Prompt Composer discovers only prompt snippets. The plugin ignores obsolete `prompt-composer.jsonc` files.

## References

Use forward-slash relative filenames with extensions. Nested includes resolve against the same discovered registry, not relative to the including file. `.md` and `.txt` are distinct names. Snippets are plain text; frontmatter is not interpreted as a name override.

Paths cannot be absolute or contain traversal, hidden segments, backslashes or control characters. Included files must be regular UTF-8 text without NUL. Symlinks contained within the prompt root are allowed. Symlinks that escape the prompt root or point to hidden paths, unreadable entries and directories past the nesting limit are ignored with a warning; directory cycles and a `prompts` path that is not a directory are ignored quietly. Ignored entries are never read.

## Limits

- Included file: 64 KiB.
- Body containing include syntax: 256 KiB before and after expansion. Marker-free native text bypasses this budget.
- Include expansion: 32 levels and 256 occurrences.
- Discovery: 4096 entries, 32 directory levels and 256 ancestor-directory iterations. Kilo checks both of its project directories in each iteration.

An include that breaks a limit is left out with a warning, and a prompt over 256 KiB keeps its native text. Past 4096 entries, discovery keeps what it found and ignores the rest with a warning. These limits apply to prompt snippets and composition, not to a settings file. See [Usage](Usage#snippet-lifetime) for when changes become visible.

# Prompt Composer

Share reusable text across native agents, commands and on-demand skills with explicit inline includes, in OpenCode and Kilo CLI. These guides describe the current repository; published packages may differ.

| Host | Package | Versions |

| OpenCode | `@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer` | [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer?activeTab=versions) |

# Migration

## From older Prompt Composer settings

Current Prompt Composer uses explicit includes in native bodies. It no longer reads `prompt-composer.jsonc`, accepts plugin options, or provides the `/compose-prompts` editor.

Move each default or per-agent prepend/append into the appropriate native agent body at the intended position. Shared guidance can live in a snippet referenced by several agents. Preserve the intended order and resolve any formerly conditional guidance explicitly; there is no prompt-profile selection mechanism.

Replace source-alias references such as `{{include:@team/review.md}}` with `{{include:review.md}}` after moving the file into a discovered `prompts/` directory. Remove obsolete settings after transferring the guidance. Keep native agent, command and skill definitions in the host's own files. [Discovery](Discovery) explains override order.

Use `/view-prompts` to inspect loaded agent prompts and command templates. Edit files in your normal editor and restart the OpenCode or Kilo server to capture new snippets. The viewer does not save or apply settings.

## Using Config Composer alongside Prompt Composer

Config Composer is an OpenCode plugin, so this section applies to the OpenCode package only. The packages are independent. Config Composer owns configuration composition; Prompt Composer owns prompt includes. When using both, register Config Composer first so Prompt Composer receives the resulting agent availability. Avoid older Config Composer releases that also expand prompts, which can expand escaped markers twice.

Compatibility testing uses an explicit Config Composer baseline; it does not establish compatibility with every Config Composer revision. See [Developer](Developer#host-compatibility) for the test policy. Configuration migration belongs in [Config Composer's documentation](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/opencode-config-composer/wiki).

Agents without a nonblank authored prompt retain native fallback. To compose guidance into such an agent, author its native prompt intentionally and place includes there.

# Publishing

The [Release workflow](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml) runs only when started by hand on `main`, and publishes only when its **publish** input is checked. It releases the workspace's one version in one run: it publishes `@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer` and `@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer` to npm in that order, creates the `v<version>` tag on the release commit once, and publishes a GitHub release for that tag with the two package tarballs attached and notes generated from the merged pull requests. Branch pushes, pull requests and tag pushes do not publish packages. The shared core in `packages/core` is private: it is bundled into both packages at build time and is never packed or published.

## Publisher setup

The workflow expects these settings, configured through the respective services. This page describes the required setup, not confirmation of its current state.

- **npm trusted publishers:** one on each of the two packages, each with organization `lunchbox-labs`, repository `prompt-composer-plugin`, workflow filename `release.yml` and environment `release`. Allow direct `npm publish`, which is the command this workflow uses. npm offers the setting only on a package that exists, so [bootstrap](#bootstrap-a-new-package-name) a package name that has never been published first. See [npm's trusted publishing guide](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/).
- **`release` environment:** allows deployments from `main` only. It holds no secrets or variables.
- **Actions policy:** only maintainers may start Release, and Wiki may run only on pushes to `main`. Both can write to the repository.
- **Tag rulesets:** a ruleset blocks updating and deleting `v*` tags. No ruleset blocks creating them, because Release creates the tag itself.

The publish job has `id-token: write` for OIDC and `contents: read`. It installs a trusted-publishing-capable npm version and enables provenance. The workflow does not use a long-lived npm token. Only the GitHub release job has `contents: write`, and it runs no repository code. Both jobs run in the `release` environment.

## Bootstrap a new package name

Verify stops a run when either package name is not on npm, before anything is published. `@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer` is already on npm, so only `@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer` needs this. To add a package name, a maintainer with publish rights in the `lunchbox-labs` npm organization publishes a placeholder of it once, under its own dist-tag. The placeholder is a bare manifest with no code and no dependencies, not the built package: npm points `latest` at a package's first version until a stable release moves it, and an install of `latest` must get a harmless placeholder, not a build that was never released. In an empty directory outside the repository:

```sh
cat > package.json <<'JSON'
{
  "name": "@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer",
  "version": "0.0.0-bootstrap.0",
  "description": "Placeholder that reserves the name; install a released version.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "repository": {
    "type": "git",
    "url": "git+https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin.git"
  }
}
JSON
npm publish --tag bootstrap --access public
npm deprecate @lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer@0.0.0-bootstrap.0 "Placeholder; install a released version."
npm dist-tag ls @lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer
```

For any later new package, use its own name. The bootstrap version is never used for a release. `npm dist-tag ls` shows where `bootstrap` and `latest` point; `latest` moves to the first stable version that Release publishes. Then add the package's trusted publisher as above. If a placeholder of `@lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-core` was ever published, leave it deprecated; no release publishes that name.

Start Release with **publish** unchecked to confirm that Verify passes. That run stops before npm, so it does not exercise the trusted publisher or OIDC. If a trusted publisher is missing or wrong, the first real run publishes the packages before that one and fails at it. Fix the publisher and re-run only the failed jobs within the artifact's three days: Publish npm skips the packages npm already holds with the same tarballs and publishes the rest.

## Prepare and run a release

1. Set the same version in `packages/opencode/package.json` and `packages/kilo/package.json`, and run `npm install` so their workspace entries in `package-lock.json` match. The private core's version is not released and need not change. Use a non-placeholder semantic version that has no tag and isn't on npm yet for either package: a stable version such as `1.2.3` for a release, or a pre-release version such as `1.2.3-beta.1` for a pre-release.
2. Complete the required checks and review, and integrate the release commit into `main` through the repository's normal process.
3. Open **Actions**, choose **Release**, and select **Run workflow** with `main` as the branch and **publish** checked. The run releases the commit at the head of `main` when it starts, so start it once the release commit is the latest commit there. Run it once per version.

The run has two inputs:

- **publish:** off by default. Unchecked, the run builds, checks and packs the release and keeps the tarballs only as the run's `release` artifact, then stops before npm, the tag and the GitHub release. It still stops at Verify when the version is already tagged or on npm. Check it to publish the official release.
- **prerelease:** publishes under npm's `next` tag instead of `latest`, and marks the GitHub release as a pre-release. A pre-release run needs a pre-release version, and a normal run a stable one, so `latest` never moves to a pre-release.

The run's summary names the version as soon as the **Release version** job finishes, and links the release once the **GitHub release** job has published it. Don't push the tag or create the release by hand: Release refuses a version that is already tagged, and tags can't be moved or deleted.

## What the run does

**Release version** stops a run started on any other branch, reads the version from the two package manifests and stops when they differ. **Verify** then requires the checked-out commit to match the run's commit, and stops before building when either package name is not on npm yet, when `v<version>` is already tagged, or when either package already has the version on npm. [validate-release.mjs](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/scripts/validate-release.mjs) also validates each package's identity, repository, registry, access and lockfile metadata, and that neither package names the private core in any dependency field. Verify runs `npm ci` and `npm run test:package`, packs the two packages and uploads the tarballs with SHA-256 checksums.

**Check** runs the [Check workflow](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml) on the release commit as part of the run, with every job it runs on a push to `main`. Its runs inside Release are grouped apart from Check's own runs, so a push to `main` during a release doesn't cancel them.

**Publish npm** downloads the verified tarballs, checks their checksums and publishes them with scripts disabled, OpenCode first, then Kilo. It does not rebuild the packages. **GitHub release** then creates the `v<version>` tag on the release commit and publishes a GitHub release for it with the same tarballs attached.

If a job fails, inspect it before retrying, and re-run only the failed jobs so the verified packages are reused. Re-running Publish npm is safe after a partial publication: it skips each package npm already holds at this version with the same tarball, publishes the rest in order, and stops at a package npm holds with a different tarball. Re-running GitHub release accepts an existing tag only on the release commit, publishes a draft left for the tag with the tarballs attached, and leaves an already published release as it is. A new run, or a full re-run, stops at verification once the version is tagged or on npm, so finish a partly failed release by re-running its failed jobs within the artifact's three days. After that, bump the version, merge it to `main` and run Release again. Keep release-specific investigation and validation evidence in the tracking issue.

# Usage

Prompt Composer expands reusable text in native agent prompts, command templates and skill-tool bodies of OpenCode and Kilo CLI. It requires Node 22.18+. The OpenCode package is tested with OpenCode 1.19.x, starting at 1.19.0, and the Kilo package with Kilo CLI 7.8.x, starting at 7.8.27. It works independently of Config Composer.

## Install

For OpenCode, add the package to `plugin` in `opencode.jsonc`, and to `tui.jsonc` for the prompt viewer:

```jsonc
{ "plugin": ["@lunchbox-labs/opencode-prompt-composer"] }
```

For Kilo CLI, add the Kilo package to `plugin` in `kilo.jsonc`, and to `tui.jsonc` for the prompt viewer:

```jsonc
{ "plugin": ["@lunchbox-labs/kilo-prompt-composer"] }
```

The rest of this page applies to both hosts. Examples use OpenCode's directories; Kilo reads `.kilocode` and `.kilo` in their place, and `~/.config/kilo` for global config, as [Discovery](Discovery) lists.

## Include reusable text

Put snippets in a `prompts/` directory, such as `.opencode/prompts/review/findings.md`. Include them at the desired position in an agent, command or skill body:

```markdown
Review the supplied changes.

{{include:review/findings.md}}

Distinguish observed behavior from assumptions.
```

References are relative `.md` or `.txt` filenames. Includes expand recursively against the same discovered prompt registry; each included file is trimmed at its edges. Surrounding text determines spacing. Write `\{{include:review/findings.md}}` to preserve a literal marker. [Discovery](Discovery) describes directory precedence, supported paths and limits.

Use `{{include?:personal/review.md}}` for optional guidance. If no discovered `prompts/` directory contains that file, the marker expands to nothing. For example, a developer can opt in by adding `~/.config/opencode/prompts/personal/review.md`. All other behavior matches `{{include:...}}`: an invalid path, an unreadable or invalid file, a cycle, or the include count or depth limit leaves that include out with a warning. Write `\{{include?:personal/review.md}}` to preserve the literal optional marker.

Keep all guidance in native bodies and snippet files. There is no Prompt Composer settings file, and plugin options are ignored with a warning. Agent metadata and command placeholders such as `$ARGUMENTS` and `$1` remain native. Disabled agents and agents with no nonblank authored prompt keep their existing text or native fallback.

Skill bodies expand when the native `skill` tool returns them. Automatically generated skill slash commands do not pass through that hook and do not expand includes; running one that contains include markers shows a warning once per skill. Skill discovery and permissions remain the host's responsibility. Kilo's built-in skills, which Kilo frames without a base directory or file list, expand too.

## Snippet lifetime

The plugin captures the project's winning snippet files when it first initializes in the server process, including snippets first used by later skill calls. Edits, additions and removals are visible after restarting that process. Instance disposal alone does not refresh snippets, except that a capture that failed is retried. Restart the OpenCode or Kilo server after editing snippets or native prompt definitions.

Include problems never stop a prompt from loading. A failing include expands to nothing, a malformed marker stays as written, and a prompt over the 256 KiB limit, or one with nothing left once failed includes are left out, keeps its native text; other agents, commands and skills compose normally. A warning toast names the consumer and shows the first problem with its logical include chain and, for nested snippets, the snippet position; the host's log lists every problem. If the prompts directories cannot be read at all, an error toast appears and everything keeps its native text. Diagnostics omit prompt bodies.

## View loaded prompts

Run `/view-prompts`, choose **Agents** or **Commands**, then select a component to read its full loaded text in a scrollable viewer. Text over 65,536 characters, or with a line over 4,096 characters, opens as a list of parts. Escape returns to the previous view. Configured agents appear by default; **Show built-in agents** includes native defaults, and the host remembers that choice. Disabled agents and native fallbacks are labeled.

The viewer shows loaded text without executing command syntax, expanding markers again, changing files or sending a model request. It omits skills because the host API does not expose their composed bodies for this view. It does not show the full model request.

## Includes and native file references

OpenCode and Kilo substitute `{file:path}` inside JSON configuration strings before plugins run. The path resolves relative to the configuration file or `~/`; the reference is not recursive, has no escape, and a missing file fails configuration loading. Use it to load one whole prompt from a file.

Includes also work inside Markdown agent, command and skill bodies. They expand recursively, resolve against discovered `prompts/` directories and accept the `\{{include:...}}` escape. A prompt loaded through `{file:}` can contain includes because the plugin receives the substituted text. Optional includes have no `{file:}` equivalent.

## Examples

Each package ships the same two examples, laid out for its host:

- Review guidance shares a findings format between an agent and command: [OpenCode](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/tree/main/packages/opencode/docs/examples/review), [Kilo](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/tree/main/packages/kilo/docs/examples/review).
- On-demand verification loads a checklist through a skill: [OpenCode](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/tree/main/packages/opencode/docs/examples/skill-guidance), [Kilo](https://github.com/lunchbox-labs/prompt-composer-plugin/tree/main/packages/kilo/docs/examples/skill-guidance).
- [Migration](Migration) covers older Prompt Composer settings and optional Config Composer ordering.
